q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of a bottle of hair oil?
title: Hair oil carbon footprint per bottle
short: Add the base oils, such as coconut or mineral oil, and perfume per bottle with supplier figures. Then add the bottle, cap and label, plus blending, filling and packing electricity divided by bottles filled. Report by pack size.
audience: Hair oil brands and contract fillers

ul: Coconut, mineral or other base oils.
HDPE or PET bottle, cap and label.

p: Report per bottle by millilitres, and per litre so packs of different sizes compare fairly.

example.title: Worked example: hair oil unit per bottle (one month)
lines: Plant total: 5,680 / 400,000 = 0.0142 kg CO2 per bottle
Add oils, bottles and caps for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
